rationale: Three lenses ran against the full diff. Every confirmed finding was fixed in-branch and re-verified live; the remaining accepted findings fail closed rather than corrupting user data, and are recorded in spec.md section 12.
business_review: Story acceptance criteria audited: all 7 primary and 4 negative criteria pass or pass-with-recorded-deviation.

Two story deviations were pre-approved by the user (surgical disconnect, marker-keyed backup); a third revision (proxy-side model resolution) and a fourth (empty tool descriptions) were approved in conversation after live testing and are recorded in spec.md sections 11 and 12.
standards_review: ESLint clean on every changed file; the single repo-wide failure (statusline.mjs) is pre-existing and identical on main, verified via a temporary worktree.
Typecheck clean, build clean, 3187 unit tests pass, gitleaks reports no leaks.

Follows the established *-request-normalizer plugin pattern; reuses writeAtomically rather than the non-atomic Kimi precedent; ConfigurationError, logger and sanitizeLogArgs used per project convention.

findings.summary: cutRegionLines deleted to EOF when a close sentinel was missing (data loss on connect or disconnect)
Sentinel matching inconsistent between reader (substring) and cutter (exact line), duplicating the managed block on a trailing space or CR
Gateway key logged in cleartext: sanitizeLogArgs does not match the key name gatewayKey
backupIfUnmanaged could snapshot an already-managed file, enshrining the bearer token as the pre-connect original
Connect never validated its own output, so any splice edge case shipped a broken config.toml
codex-desktop missing from CodexEncryptedContentSanitizerPlugin allowlist, silently disabling Responses reasoning-state handling the spec relies on
Substitution fallback could reroute a Responses request to a Claude or embedding deployment
Disconnect verified only that the strip parsed, not that CodeMie keys were gone
Unbounded recursion and no cycle guard on a client-controlled request body
Failed model listing was never cached, causing a per-request fetch storm against a broken gateway
Date pattern end-anchored, so a suffix after the release date reintroduced the date-as-version inversion
Resolver took the gateway's first identity match rather than the newest
--model rejected the undated names the app picker displays and the proxy resolves
Combining --codex-desktop with a higher-priority target silently disabled Codex model resolution
No timeout on the connect-time model listing
Config path printed only under --verbose, contradicting the docs
Unsupported platform rendered as 'Looked in: .'; disconnect errors went to stdout
Missing or non-binding tests required by spec section 8 (atomic-write failure, write ordering, app-detection writes nothing)
isTableHeader is not TOML-aware (multi-line strings and arrays); now fails closed via output validation rather than corrupting
Quoted root keys not recognized as displaceable; fails closed via output validation
Concurrent connect/disconnect on the same file is unserialized
Real per-platform app-candidate paths untested; Windows locations should be checked against a real install, with --force as the escape hatch

false_positives: writeAtomically was claimed not to preserve file mode; it does, defaulting to 0o600 for new files.
isCodexCompatibleModel was claimed not to filter disabled models; it does.

The codex-desktop client type was claimed never to reach ProxyConfig, making the plugin dead code; disproved by runtime evidence (daemon state shows clientType codex-desktop and live model resolution works).
